title: First 13 Weeks Adoption Roadmap + Risk Cards
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a modular, engineer-forward 13-week adoption roadmap for new Redwood Inference customers. It focuses on predictable time-to-first-value, measurable usage milestones, and headroom for performance tuning. Use this as a baseline for medium-to-large customers (PLG-to-enterprise) and adapt sections by customer size and risk profile.

How to use this doc:
- Run the chapters as weekly sprints (Weeks 1–13).
- Share the relevant sections with the customer during weekly check-ins.
- Attach ‘Risk Cards’ to the customer record and update as issues are discovered.
- Track renewal signals at the bottom and escalate at defined thresholds.

Executive summary (one-liner):
Drive habitual usage by week 6 and reach stable production performance and cost targets by week 13.

Success criteria (sample, measurable):
- Integration: Successful API key exchange + sample inference call within first 3 days.
- Adoption: 3 distinct product teams issuing inference calls by day 30.
- Stability: 95th percentile latency under target for 72 hours by week 8.
- ROI: Token cost per successful request within agreed threshold by week 13.
- Renewal signal: Sustained monthly token consumption >= 50% of committed capacity for two consecutive months.

Kickoff checklist (Day 0–3):
- Confirm point-of-contact list and escalation paths.
- API credentials generated and validated (CS to confirm).
- Minimum viable integration: dev team runs a successful generation + embedding call.
- Baseline metrics snapshot: initial token usage, latency, error rate, infra quotas.
- If private/dedicated: ensure VPN/VPC and KMS keys are provisioned.

13-week breakdown (by week):
Week 1: Orientation + quick wins
- Deliverables: kickoff deck, feature map, urgent-asks list.
- Action: Walkthrough of Redwood Console (routes, quotas, telemetry).
- Target: First successful end-to-end call from a dev sandbox.
- Meeting: 60-min kickoff w/ product engineer + CSM.

Week 2: Integration hardening
- Deliverables: integration checklist, sample prompt templates, retry/backoff guidance.
- Action: Instrument basic telemetry for token counts and error codes.
- Target: Error rate < 5% on test suite.

Week 3: Early adopters & evaluation set
- Deliverables: prioritized feature list for pilot teams, evaluation prompts, eval harness link.
- Action: Run A/B prompt tests for top 3 use cases.
- Target: Baseline quality metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate) captured.

Week 4: Data ingestion & tooling
- Deliverables: embeddings pipeline plan, chunking rules, datastore mapping.
- Action: Start ingesting a sample dataset to embedding index.
- Target: Retrieval times within expected bounds; embedding recall spot-check.

Week 5: Load shaping & batching
- Deliverables: batching configuration, suggested KV cache settings, cost estimate.
- Action: Run synthetic loads to observe batching behavior and latency.
- Target: Identify a production-friendly batch size with acceptable p95 latency.

Week 6: Adoption milestone (habit formation)
- Deliverables: usage play for internal stakeholders, training materials.
- Action: Host a hands-on workshop for product teams integrating API.
- Target: 50% of pilot users running daily calls.

Week 7: Performance tuning
- Deliverables: tuning checklist (quantization options, kernel hints), model variant recommendations.
- Action: Test model variants (faster/cheaper) and measure quality delta.
- Target: Achieve cost/latency balance for production route.

Week 8: Reliability & observability
- Deliverables: alerting thresholds, SLO definitions, trace capture plan.
- Action: Configure trace hooks and error grouping in Console.
- Target: SLO alert pages and runbooks available.

Week 9: Security & compliance review
- Deliverables: data flow diagram, audit log config, KMS key rotation plan.
- Action: Conduct a checklist walkthrough with customer's security contact.
- Target: Sign-off on compliance requirements for the planned usage.

Week 10: Scale rehearsal
- Deliverables: scale runbook, spike plan, fallback strategies.
- Action: Do an orchestrated spike test and validate fallback behavior (model variant, region failover).
- Target: No critical failures; fallback paths exercised.

Week 11: Business metrics alignment
- Deliverables: usage to business outcome map, KPI dashboard.
- Action: Joint session to map product metrics to business outcomes (ex: leads per 1k tokens).
- Target: Agreement on metrics to report in QBR.

Week 12: Renewal health check & enablement
- Deliverables: renewal playbook draft, contract utilization snapshot, adoption summary.
- Action: Identify gaps vs. committed capacity and list mitigations.
- Target: Present renewal health to customer and internal AE/CS lead.

Week 13: Production handoff + closure
- Deliverables: production runbook, operational contacts, training recordings.
- Action: Formal handoff meeting; close sprint cycle and create follow-up ops ticket.
- Target: Customer marked as ‘live’ and eligible for Dedicated/Reserved capacity conversation.

Risk Cards (attach to customer record; update as discovered)
- Risk: Low dev bandwidth
  Impact: Delays to integration and adoption.
  Mitigation: Offer engineering hours (2–3 days) or pair-program session in week 2–3.
- Risk: Data ingestion complexity (large doc store / PII)
  Impact: Slower embedding rollout, compliance blockers.
  Mitigation: Provide template ETL scripts, recommend pseudonymization, escalate to security.
- Risk: Unexpected latency at scale
  Impact: UX regressions, loss of trust.
  Mitigation: Run scale rehearsal early; switch to smaller model variant + caching; prioritize KV cache.
- Risk: Cost overshoot vs expectations
  Impact: Finance frustration -> renewal risk.
  Mitigation: Weekly cost snapshots, enable Optimize recommendations, set throttles.

Renewal / Upsell signals (monitor weekly):
- Usage velocity: tokens/week trending up >= 15% for 4 weeks.
- Breadth: >2 product teams actively using platform.
- SLA alignment: production latency within target and incident rate low.
- Feature dependency: Customer builds proprietary feature that requires Reserved capacity.
- Exec engagement: Bi-weekly sponsor touchpoints ongoing.

Escalation thresholds (examples):
- Trigger AE handoff when monthly committed utilization >= 70% and growth trend positive.
- Trigger engineering support when p95 latency breaches target for >6 hours.
- Trigger renewal enablement deck when week 10 utilization >= 40% of committed capacity.

Weekly CS sync template (15–30 min)
- Quick status (green/amber/red) on integration, usage, cost, security.
- Blockers and action items.
- Top metric(s) slice for the week.
- Next actions and owner.

Sample customer email snippets
- Post-kickoff (Day 1): "Thanks for joining the kickoff — attached is the integration checklist and sandbox details. Please ping me with your sandbox test id when you complete the first call so we can validate together."
- Mid-pilot nudge (Week 4): "Quick check — saw sample embeddings finished; would you like a short review session to validate retrieval quality?"
- Renewal health (Week 12): "Attaching your utilization snapshot and suggested actions to reach production cost targets before renewal review."

Hand-off artifacts to SRE/Platform (on production)
- Stable route configuration, model versions, autoscaling policy, burst rules.
- Trace samples for recent incidents, alert history.
- Security artifacts: KMS key IDs, audit log retention policy.

Example KPI dashboard fields (for QBR)
- Total tokens consumed (month)
- Average cost per successful request
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route
- Error rate by error code
- Active product teams and daily active callers
- Embedding retrieval recall@5

Templates and artifacts to attach
- Integration checklist (CSV)
- Sample prompt bank (MD)
- Eval harness link + initial results (CSV)
- Renewal health one-pager (PDF)

Open questions to capture in week 1
- Do you have a clearly defined success metric for the integration?
- Any compliance guardrails that would change ingestion approach?
- Which teams own cost vs feature ROI?
